title: Factory Pattern
description: Create objects without specifying exact classes.

data.text: The Factory pattern creates objects without specifying the exact class. It promotes loose coupling and extensibility.

data.title: Factory in TypeScript

data.text: A factory is a function that returns an object, hiding which concrete type it built and how. Callers depend on the returned interface, so adding a new variant does not change any call site. It is the natural alternative to a constructor that has grown a switch statement.

data.title: A factory that hides construction

data.text: The same idea applied to tests is a factory that builds a valid object with sensible defaults that you override per test. It keeps tests short and makes the one field under test obvious, while a single change to the defaults updates every test.

data.title: A test data factory
Factory vs constructor vs builder
data.text: A constructor is right when there is one shape and no decisions. A factory is right when the caller should not know the concrete type. A builder is right when an object has many optional parts and the call would otherwise be a long positional argument list. Naming when each applies is more useful than memorizing one.

terms.definition: Function or class that creates objects.
